To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phase field method can be used to study phase separation in elastic materials, and that the phase field model can be used to predict the morphology of phase separated structures in elastic materials.

(a) the interaction energies are the key to understanding the effect of elastic interactions on phase separation; (b) the interaction energies can be computed from the elastic constants and the misfit strain; (c) the interaction energies provide a powerful tool to design nanostructures with desired properties; (d) the interaction energies depend strongly on the elastic constants of the system, and in particular, on the elastic heterogeneity; (e) elastic heterogeneity can be used to design structures with desired properties;
the phase separation in a solid solution is driven by the chemical free energy, and that elastic fields can be used to guide the phase separation and the formation of nanostructures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the effects of external mechanical fields on phase separation and microstructure in solids and thin films.
the fundamental aspects of self-assembly and the role of elasticity in this process.
the design of nanostructures by self-assembly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
elastic interactions are important in phase separation, and that the elastic interactions are strongly influenced by the elastic properties of the alloy.

the elastic energy is a very important factor in determining phase separation in thin films, and the elastic interaction energy between two particles can be estimated using the Eshelby method, which is useful for understanding the phase separation process.
the phase separation in the presence of external load is a complex phenomenon, which can be understood and predicted only if the elastic energy is included.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phase-field model provides a useful framework for studying the effects of elastic properties on the kinetics and morphologies of phase separation, and that the Eshelby theory of elastic interactions provides useful estimates for the effects of elastic heterogeneity and transformation strain on the kinetics and morphology of aggregation in the bulk and in thin-film systems.
we have developed a phase-field model for solid-solid phase separation, which incorporates the effects of elastic heterogeneity and externally imposed loads.
the elastic energy can be a very powerful tool in guiding self-assembly of materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, physically based model can provide a good understanding of the coupling between elastic properties and the phase separation process.
the phase-field model, coupled with a simple energy analysis, provides a powerful tool for predicting the effects of elastic interactions on phase separation and self-organization.
the elastic energy can be manipulated via external fields and can play a key role in the self-assembly of micro- and nanostructure.
